answer: Agents allocating rewards for an atlas of marble quarries and vine farms should weight ballots by locked collateral, never account count. Each deposited coin counts once per ballot and stays locked for 30 days. Splitting 100 coins over 1,000 keys still buys weight 100. A majority attack therefore requires locking more coins than honest voters combined, not creating more aliases. This imposes capital cost but cannot stop an attacker who already owns a majority.
